Subject: Request: On-prem VPC integration & control/data separation — Zephyr pilot

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the quick intro call last week. ZephyrCloud is moving forward with a small pilot to evaluate Redwood's private VPC (on-prem) deployment for inference workloads. Before we lock down procurement and rack scheduling, the infra team asked for an architecture review focused on control plane / data plane demarcation, egress attestations, and minimal NAT/egress requirements.

Attached is a rough sketch (zephyr_vpc_sketch.pdf) and a spreadsheet of workloads and expected traffic patterns (redwood_control_data_matrix.xlsx). High-level constraints from our side:
- No outbound public IPs from tenant runtime. Egress must go through a controlled NAT cluster in our colo.
- Control plane endpoints must be reachable over mTLS from the management VPC (10.200.0.0/16).
- We require audit log forwarding to our SIEM (syslog over TLS) and a KMS integration option for key usage audit.
- Latency: <50ms for control calls between control plane and management APIs.

We want to make sure the control plane can be logically separated from the inference data plane and that deployment patterns align with our security/compliance needs. Would you and your infra architects be available for a 30-min technical review this week (Wed/Thu)?

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Lead SRE, ZephyrCloud

Thanks for the sketch, Alex — a few technical clarifications ahead of Thu's call to make the review productive:

1) Control plane reachability
- Do you expect the control plane to initiate connections into the customer's management VPC, or will the customer route a static route/NAT so that customer-managed agents reach Redwood control endpoints? Our usual pattern is: customer side makes egress TLS connections to Redwood control endpoints, authenticated with mTLS and short-lived certs. If Zephyr prefers inbound, we need a secure ingress path and an HA load balancer in your management VPC.

2) mTLS and cert provisioning
- Can Zephyr accept a CA-signed cert from Redwood for the pilot, or do you require customer-managed certs via your internal PKI? If internal PKI is required, we'll need a cadence for cert rotation and an API to upload public certs.

3) Egress/NAT and telemetry
- You mention syslog over TLS. Will syslog collectors be reachable from the runtime clusters over the NAT egress? If the runtime cannot have public IPs and must egress via your NAT, we'll need a small egress allowlist (FQDNs/IPs) for Redwood telemetry and control endpoints. Please list any deny-lists or strict ACLs.

4) KV cache & stateful artifacts
- For the pilot, do you want our KV cache persisted to local SAN, or should we build an ephemeral cache with warm starts from your object store? Persisted KV influences storage and fencing requirements.

5) Sizing
- Please provide target concurrency and any burst patterns (token/sec) for the models you plan to run. This influences reserved GPU sizing and whether we recommend colocated model variants to reduce cross-subnet egress.

If you can reply inline to the questions above or drop answers into the attached spreadsheet, we'll prepare a concise architecture proposal for Thu.

-Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Architecture review notes — Zephyr pilot

Alex / Zephyr folks — thanks for the call today. Quick meeting notes and agreed actions so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of decisions
- Control plane pattern: Zephyr will allow outbound mTLS from a dedicated Management NAT pool (10.200.1.0/28) to Redwood control endpoints. No inbound public IPs required.
- Cert model: Zephyr will provide customer-managed public certs (internal PKI). Redwood will accept uploaded public certs via a secure API for the pilot.
- Egress & telemetry: Runtime clusters will egress through your NAT; Zephyr to add the following allowlist entries to the NAT ACLs: redwood-control.redwood.internal (IP: 52.33.120.10), telemetry.redwood.internal (IP: 52.33.120.11).
- KV cache behavior: For the pilot we'll run ephemeral KV cache with warm-ups from Zephyr object storage (S3-compatible). If pilot shows heavy cold-start penalties, we'll revisit local persistence.
- Sizing: Zephyr provided target peak concurrency of ~120 sessions and burst to 300 tokens/sec. We agreed a single p4d-equivalent reserved pool will be provisioned for the pilot; Redwood will send a sizing confirmation doc.

Action items (owners & due dates)
- Zephyr (Alex): Share exact NAT IP pool and ACL export by Tue 2026-06-15. (ACTION: Alex)
- Jordan: Produce short architecture diagram (control/data arrows, NAT demarcation) and a recommended ACL minimal list. Deliver by Fri 2026-06-12. (ACTION: Jordan)
- Karthik: Draft runtime sizing confirmation and a note on KV cache tradeoffs. Deliver by Fri 2026-06-12. (ACTION: Karthik)
- Naomi: Confirm telemetry forwarding options and ingestion tests with Zephyr SIEM. Deliver by Mon 2026-06-14. (ACTION: Naomi)
